instances.claim: This tells me that there is a bounded, countable set of individual objects, each one called a Cent, and that the draft has already shown me what that set is and that its membership is fixed.
instances.why: "Every Cent" quantifies over a population whose existence and boundaries the draft never establishes: line 1 names "the penny" as a reproduced artwork, line 5 says "a cent" generically, and the title CENTS does not appear until line 21 — so at line 8 nothing has introduced a collection of discrete Cents for "every" to range over. Lines 9–13 then make claims about the life of a single member of that uncounted set, which only reads as coherent if the set had been introduced.

instances.claim: This tells me that the object had been destroyed, dematerialized, or otherwise stripped of physical existence, and that it persisted anyway.
instances.why: "Remained" and "buoyed into physicality" are continuation and recovery claims — both presuppose a prior state in which the object's survival or materiality was in doubt. Lines 4–6 put only monetary value in doubt, never the object's physical persistence, and the only destruction in the draft (line 12) comes five lines later, so at line 7 there is nothing for "remained" to have remained against.
